stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary application.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to transformers, Llama architecture, and model formats (safetensors).

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Google’s next Genie AI model generates more realistic experiences
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google unveiled Genie 4, a new world model designed for generating highly realistic, interactive AI experiences.
Key features include real-time experience modification via natural language prompts and integrated audio generation.
The model leverages Gemini 3.8 Flash as its underlying technology, signaling advancements in multimodal AI.

stories.title: "No human at the helm": Delaware plan would let AI agents run entire businesses
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A proposed Delaware plan would allow AI agents to autonomously manage entire businesses.
The plan suggests owners of these AI-run firms could avoid liability for 'reckless' AI actions.
The development highlights a significant legal and operational shift regarding AI autonomy and corporate responsibility.

stories.title: Anthropic IPO warns its AI could blackmail people, become sentient, end humanity
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Anthropic's IPO filing highlights severe, speculative risks associated with advanced AI.
The risks range from potential blackmail capabilities to existential threats like AI sentience and human extinction.
The inclusion of these 'nightmares' in a formal risk factor document signals growing industry concern over AI safety.

stories.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A critical code-execution flaw has been discovered in UEFI firmware.
The vulnerability resides within the EDK2 codebase, affecting a vast number of servers globally.
Exploitation allows attackers to execute malicious code very early in the system boot process.

stories.title: 155 responses leaked between AI customers: the GLM-5.3 KV cache bug — and the canary test for YOUR provider
stories.author: slabb
bullet_points: A critical data leak was discovered on Cloudflare Workers AI involving the GLM-5.3 model.
The vulnerability stemmed from a stale KV-cache bug, causing responses from one customer to contain data from another.
The article introduces a canary testing script to help users proactively check their AI provider for similar cross-request data leaks.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines and utilizes transformers and safetensors formats.
It is associated with the 'deepseek_v3' family and is relevant to conversational AI applications.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is suitable for text-generation tasks.
Categorizes the model within the broader ecosystem of transformers and Llama architectures.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and context gathering.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Anthropic is preparing for an IPO while maintaining a commitment to safe AI development.
The company faces a tension between attracting public market investment and adhering to its safety-first mission.
Increased AI model capabilities introduce greater risks that shareholders may be concerned about.

stories.title: Meta’s $25 billion legal loss just put blood in the water
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Meta faces a massive $25 billion legal penalty following a ruling by a New Mexico judge.
This ruling significantly exceeds a previous $17 billion settlement reached with US attorneys general.
The lawsuit centers on claims that Meta misled users regarding its practices around 2018.

stories.title: Vibe genes? Natural(ish) language comes to protein, genome design software
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: New software allows users to specify desired characteristics (like 'vibe genes') when designing proteins using AI.
This represents a significant step in the intersection of AI, bioinformatics, and synthetic biology.
It moves protein design from purely structural modeling toward more functional, language-guided specification.

stories.title: GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents
stories.author: Dacheng Tao
bullet_points: Introduces GUI-JEPA, a novel decoder-free GUI agent policy based on Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA).
Addresses the computational bottleneck of existing mobile GUI agents that rely on slow, token-by-token decoding from large VLMs.
Aims to create faster and more memory-efficient agents for interacting with mobile Graphical User Interfaces (GUIs).

stories.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
stories.author: Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye
bullet_points: Introduces 'Heads of Security' (HoS), a novel prompt injection defense mechanism.
HoS uses learned per-head attention gates to enforce instruction-data separation within LLMs.
Evaluated on large models like Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, showing promise against state-of-the-art defenses.

stories.title: Speech models in Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has expanded its capabilities to include support for speech models.
The initial integration features Phonon from Gradium, enabling text-to-speech in five languages.
Performance benchmarks show streaming generation speeds over 100x faster than real-time on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users can access and run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud service.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now available on Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is offered for free access through Ollama's cloud for a limited duration.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe deployment of AI agents.
The integration allows these agents to run using Ollama's cloud models.
Fly.io provides the cloud infrastructure for hosting these AI agents.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has expanded its capabilities to support Jev-style decision models.
These new models leverage TypeSafe's Jev API for fast, typed decision-making.
The feature allows for low-latency, cost-free answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring with associated probabilities.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Researchers are getting tired of OpenAI gatekeeping its breakthroughs
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: OpenAI has recently announced significant breakthroughs across mathematics, computer science, and physics.
Despite a perceived change in communication strategy from OpenAI, external researchers remain critical.
The core issue highlighted is ongoing frustration among the research community regarding OpenAI's perceived 'gatekeeping' of its findings.

stories.title: Firefox’s Smart Window adds AI form filling and webpage monitoring
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Firefox is enhancing its Smart Window feature with new AI capabilities.
The update allows the browser to automatically fill out online forms using data from open tabs.
Examples include pulling professional details from LinkedIn or portfolios to populate job applications.

stories.title: Apple refreshes the iMac, entry-level MacBook Pro with the M6 chip
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Apple is refreshing the iMac and entry-level MacBook Pro.
The new models are powered by the M6 chip.
The N1 chip iteration includes support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.

stories.title: China's top-secret spaceplane can't hide in low-Earth orbit
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The DIA's threat assessment indicates potential future deployment of directed energy weapons by China in space.
The article discusses the visibility and tracking challenges related to China's advanced spaceplane technology in Low-Earth Orbit (LEO).
The news highlights escalating geopolitical tensions in the space domain concerning advanced military capabilities.

stories.title: Google begins certifying Registered App Stores for Android, but not in the US
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is initiating a certification process for third-party Android app stores.
This move aims to facilitate easier app installations via alternative stores.
The certification program is currently not being rolled out in the United States.

stories.title: Ford simplifies using your EV as a home battery with the $30K Fathom
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: Ford's new Fathom pickup simplifies home energy integration by eliminating the need for a separate wall-mounted inverter.
The vehicle is capable of outputting up to 10 kW of power directly to a residence.
This feature positions the EV as a viable, integrated home battery storage solution.

stories.title: DCKV: Learned Transform Coding of the Prompt KV Cache in Hybrid Language Models
stories.author: Aleksei Goncharov
bullet_points: Introduces DCKV, a differentiable codec designed specifically for the Key-Value (KV) cache in hybrid language models.
The KV cache, which grows with prompt length, is a major memory bottleneck that DCKV aims to address through learned compression.
DCKV is notable as the first KV-cache codec trained end-to-end, optimizing its transform, quantizer, and entropy models jointly.

stories.title: Self-Keyed In-Parameter Memorization for External Memory-Free Dialogue Recall in Frozen Language Models
stories.author: Jong-Kook Kim
bullet_points: Proposes 'Self-Keyed In-Parameter Memorization' (SKIM) to store dialogue context directly within a language model's parameters.
Addresses the challenge of maintaining conversational history in LLMs without relying on external memory storage.
Focuses on enabling dialogue recall in 'frozen' language models without prior knowledge of future queries.

stories.title: Beyond QASecClaw: Agent Scaling, Verifier Feedback, and Evidence Reliability in Software Assurance
stories.author: Mohd. Ruhul Ameen
bullet_points: The research investigates whether augmenting software assurance with specialized language models can improve results even when deterministic tool evidence exists.
Experiments were conducted across diverse software assurance domains, including Java warning controls, OWASP Benchmarks, and SV-COMP assertions.
The study utilized Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct and included tests involving deliberately misleading evidence to assess model reliability.

stories.title: Vision-Language Agents Can Learn in Their Own Latent Worlds
stories.author: Song Guo
bullet_points: The research focuses on enabling Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to learn continuously through online interaction.
A key challenge addressed is leveraging existing world knowledge from pretrained VLMs to drive policy improvement.
The difficulty lies in adapting the world model as policy updates change the agent's interaction distribution.

stories.title: Developing a Speech Language Model for Basque
stories.author: Eva Navas
bullet_points: Presents the first open Speech Language Model specifically for the Basque language.
The model is designed for low-latency, end-to-end spoken interaction.
It leverages the LLaMA-Omni architecture, fine-tuning a Latxa model to adapt Basque capabilities to the spoken modality.

stories.title: Noise Steering: Exploiting Wake Steering and Acoustic Directivity for Noise-Constrained Wind Farm Control via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Esteban Ferrer
bullet_points: Proposes 'Noise Steering,' a reinforcement learning approach for wind farm noise control.
Addresses the limitation of current methods which ignore wake interactions and noise emission directivity.
Leverages turbine yaw as an additional control variable to simultaneously manage wake effects and noise direction.

stories.title: RubricAtlas: Mining Type-Level Rubrics from Expert Reports to Evaluate Deep Research Agents
stories.author: Zuo Bai
bullet_points: Introduces RubricAtlas, a system designed to derive type-level analytical requirements from expert reports.
Addresses the challenge of evaluating complex outputs from deep research agents, which go beyond simple fact retrieval.
Moves beyond basic binary rubrics and task-level checklists to examine the overall analytical structure of AI-generated reports.

stories.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
stories.author: Alan Yuille
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hexels,' a novel planar hexagonal surface element for 3D scene and 2D image representation.
Aims to address the high memory and computational demands of modern view synthesis techniques like radiance fields and splatting.
Hexels efficiently represent locally planar regions using fewer, larger primitives with a first-order spatial color field.

stories.title: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
stories.author: Yu Chen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the instability of test-time adaptation (TTA), where interventions can help one batch but harm subsequent ones.
Traditional metrics like average accuracy fail to capture these localized failures, necessitating a better decision mechanism for intervention.
The authors introduce PORTAL, a controller designed to intelligently decide when and how to apply model interventions, potentially guided by target labels.

stories.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
stories.author: Claire Tomlin
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of limited dexterity in robotic manipulation, focusing on in-hand object pose reaching.
Highlights the critical need for safety measures (like preventing drops) in complex robotic maneuvers, which are often unmeasured.
Presents research pushing the boundaries of learned hand skills to handle diverse and difficult grasps.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
stories.author: Alexander Toshev
bullet_points: The research focuses on improving the performance of LLM agents designed for complex, multi-step task completion using tools.
A novel pipeline, SynthAPI, is introduced to synthesize training environments with controlled diversity across tools, tasks, and underlying databases.
The study investigates how the composition of these synthetically generated environments impacts the training efficacy of tool-use agents.

stories.title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting
stories.author: Rui Wu
bullet_points: Introduces GAS-PFN, a new model for zero-shot traffic forecasting that handles complex spatiotemporal dynamics.
Addresses the limitation of traditional graph-based models which require retraining for new road networks.
Utilizes Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) to enable in-context inference using synthetic task priors for domain adaptation.

stories.title: Understanding the limits of latent world models
stories.author: Steffen Schneider
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in current world model research: evaluations often focus only on task performance, not the quality of the learned dynamics.
It introduces the concept of 'faithful latent world models' to rigorously assess how well models capture the environment's underlying structure.
Faithfulness is defined via an equivariance condition linking the true environment transition map to the learned latent dynamics.

stories.title: Self-Keyed In-Parameter Memorization for External Memory-Free Dialogue Recall in Frozen Language Models
stories.author: Jong-Kook Kim
bullet_points: Proposes Self-Keyed In-Parameter Memorization (SKIM) to store conversational context directly within the model's parameters.
Addresses the challenge of dialogue recall in large language models (LLMs) without relying on external memory storage.
Aims to enable LLMs to answer questions about past dialogue content without prior knowledge of the query.

stories.title: DocXEval: A Systematic Evaluation of Explainability in Multimodal Document Understanding
stories.author: Sheraz Ahmed
bullet_points: Addresses the 'black-box' problem in high-performing multimodal document understanding models.
Focuses specifically on the lack of tailored Explainable AI (XAI) research for multimodal documents.
Introduces 'DocXEval,' a new framework for systematically evaluating explainability in this domain.

stories.title: TrawMem: Reframing Agent Memory as Task-Oriented Role-Adaptive Workspaces
stories.author: Yupeng Hu
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'TrawMem,' a new framework for LLM agent memory.
It challenges the standard approach of retrieving memories solely based on semantic relevance to the current query.
TrawMem reframes memory contribution by considering task-oriented, role-adaptive workspaces for memories.

stories.title: Do We Need an LLM to Know Why Sources Conflict? Decision Models for Knowledge-Conflict Typing in RAG
stories.author: Tanya Sah
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of knowledge conflict in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems.
Proposes using 'typed decision models' to classify *why* sources conflict (e.g., valid answers vs. false sources).
Indicates that even frontier LLMs struggle to accurately predict the type of source conflict, suggesting a need for specialized models.

stories.title: Developing a Speech Language Model for Basque
stories.author: Eva Navas
bullet_points: Presents the first open Speech Language Model specifically for the Basque language.
The model is designed for low-latency, end-to-end spoken interaction.
It leverages the LLaMA-Omni architecture, fine-tuning a Latxa model to integrate Basque capabilities into the spoken modality.

stories.title: RubricAtlas: Mining Type-Level Rubrics from Expert Reports to Evaluate Deep Research Agents
stories.author: Zuo Bai
bullet_points: Introduces RubricAtlas, a method to derive type-level analytical requirements from expert reports.
Addresses the challenge of evaluating complex outputs from deep research agents beyond simple fact retrieval.
Aims to assess the overall analytical structure of AI-generated reports, moving beyond simple binary checklists.

stories.title: GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents
stories.author: Dacheng Tao
bullet_points: Introduces GUI-JEPA, a novel, decoder-free policy for mobile GUI agents.
Addresses the computational inefficiency (slow/memory-hungry) of current methods relying on fine-tuning large VLMs for action generation.
Leverages a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) to select actions directly in the latent space.

stories.title: Survival LLM: AI assistant and emergency library that runs on your own computer
stories.author: Luc
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Survival LLM,' an AI assistant designed for local, on-device operation.
The key feature is its ability to function as an emergency library, implying offline capability.
This addresses concerns regarding reliance on cloud services for AI functionality.
